products.description:
Classify, protect, and retain your data with Microsoft Purview — the right way

Sensitive data leaks and compliance gaps almost always trace back to the same root: data that isn't classified, protected, or retained. Microsoft Purview fixes that — but rolled out carelessly, labels confuse users, DLP floods the help desk with false positives, and retention either deletes too much or nothing at all. This solution gives you a repeatable way to implement Microsoft Purview information protection: a sane sensitivity-label taxonomy with auto-labeling, DLP policies that start in audit and tune before they enforce, and retention/records that meet compliance without surprises.

Run it yourself — simpler, cheaper, and proven

You do not need a consultant. The package hands you the field-tested method as self-guided, click-by-click documentation a competent admin can follow end to end — backed by ready-to-run PowerShell.

  • Simpler — exact, ordered steps with full navigation paths; every object you create is named and reused through testing and troubleshooting.
  • Cheaper — one fixed price instead of an open meter; a comparable consulting engagement runs well into the thousands per day. Reusable on every rollout.
  • Tested — a pilot-first method (Assess → Configure → Pilot → Validate → Expand) with explicit pass/fail gates.

What's inside

  • Solution Overview — the Purview information-protection model (sensitivity labels + label policies + auto-labeling, DLP across M365/endpoints, retention labels/policies and records management), and how they work together.
  • Requirements Guide — every prerequisite (Microsoft 365 + Purview licensing, Entra ID, a label taxonomy, data owners, a pilot scope, change control) with how to verify and how to implement each if missing.
  • Implementation Guide — exact, ordered steps: design the label taxonomy, publish labels and label policies, configure auto-labeling, build DLP policies in audit and tune, set retention labels/policies and records, pilot, validate, then expand.
  • 5 PowerShell scripts — Purview configuration discovery, label/DLP/retention coverage validation, a classification + DLP-event report, safe remediation of gaps, and a protection-scope group builder.
  • Testing & Troubleshooting Guides with explicit pass/fail gates, plus field-proven Best Practices for the assign-once, repeat-everywhere model.

The repeatable way

Every solution follows the same repeatable shape, so each deployment feels familiar and low-risk — buy once, reuse the playbook for the next wave and the next project.

The bottom line

Data classified, protected, and retained with Microsoft Purview — a clear label taxonomy with auto-labeling, DLP tuned in audit before it enforces, and retention that meets compliance without over- or under-deleting — proven on a pilot before you scale.

What you receive — every file in your download

This package is delivered as downloadable files you keep and reuse across unlimited devices — nothing is left out and nothing else is required:

  • Implementation Guide (PDF) — the complete, click-by-click solution: solution overview, requirements, step-by-step implementation, testing & validation, troubleshooting, best practices.
  • PowerShell Scripts (ZIP) — 5 ready-to-run scripts (read-only discovery/validation/reporting; remediation defaults to a safe preview):
    • PURVIEW-Discovery.ps1 — inventory sensitivity labels, DLP policies, and retention config
    • PURVIEW-Remediation.ps1 — safely fix common Purview configuration gaps (default -WhatIf)
    • PURVIEW-Report.ps1 — classification + DLP-event coverage report
    • PURVIEW-Set-ScopeTargeting.ps1 — build the pilot / protection-scope Entra security groups
    • PURVIEW-Validation.ps1 — confirm the expected labels, DLP, and retention objects exist

Delivered as a Word document and PDF, plus all PowerShell scripts in a single ZIP — yours to keep and reuse.

Government / GCC High tenant? A dedicated Government (GCC High) edition of this solution is available — authored for the US sovereign cloud (correct *.us portals, US Gov Graph endpoints, and Commercial-vs-GCC-High feature parity gaps called out).
